name: Cuerda seca
summary: A line of grease and manganese oxide is drawn round each colour field on an unfired tile, so that the coloured glazes do not run into each other. The line fires to a matt dark edge.
how: Draw the design on the biscuit tile.
Trace each outline with a mix of grease and manganese oxide.
Fill each field with a different glaze.
Fire the tile so that the grease burns out and leaves a dark, matt line.

origin.note: Potters in Iran and in Islamic Spain use a resist line to keep glaze colours apart on wall tiles.

adoptions.via: Seville tile makers use cuerda seca for tile panels with coloured glazes before the painted maiolica tile takes over.
